findings.finding: The scenario.symmetry.a.volume justification calls 50 Mt the RKAB-approved capacity; S3 (ANTARA, 6 April 2026) reports the RKAB was approved at 49.5 Mt without volume cuts and quotes management hoping to reach 50 Mt, so 50 Mt is the company's stated ceiling, not the approved volume. The asymmetry itself is sourced, is conservative for the bull, and carries no value effect.

Carried from round-1 Q5: unit costs are flat in nominal through FY2030E (escalation starts FY2031E), about a 10-13% real decline at 2.5% IDR inflation. Section 3 discloses this as the more optimistic reading, but it remains the one unsourced-optimistic departure in the base; the flat tail royalty is the other and is sized at about a tenth of the DCF in section 4.

flags.message: FY+1 priced at FY2025A benchmark and volume gives EBITDA 4,138.8 vs the actual 5,222.2 (-21%): reconcile costs, royalty or realisation with the filing, or justify the change
flags.justification: The actual is the LK's own EBITDA, restated off the filing: operating profit (Laba usaha) Rp3,208.073bn (F28, S5 p.17) plus the segment-note D&A of Rp2,014.102bn (F7, S5 p.159) = Rp5,222.175bn; the data pack's Rp4,961.4bn was its operating-profit fragment, which is not the LK line. Re-priced at FY2025A's benchmark (Newcastle US$108.4/t), volume (45.43 Mt), realisation (0.5175, F13/F1) and the FY2025A rupiah (16,448), the model gives EBITDA of about Rp5,108bn against the LK's Rp5,222.2bn, -2.2%: the residual is the cost split, which is re-derived on the 5.63x strip and the 9M-2026 run-rate with the FY2026E fuel term, not on the FY2025A brent (C8), and is inside model tolerance. The gate's headline -21% gap is wider for two sourced reasons, not a mis-specified history: it prices FY2025A's volume and benchmark at the FY2026E realised ratio 0.471 measured on the 9M-2026 print (F35/F36/S11) and translates at the deck's weaker FY2026E rupiah (17,570), both of which are the current forecast year, not the last actual's own conditions. Judge round 1 asked for the cost/royalty/realisation reconciliation to the filing, so here it is line by line: FY2025A cost of revenues Rp36,394,624m (S5 p.128) less royalties to government Rp4,322,659m (F11) less in-COGS D&A of depreciation Rp1,575,007m plus amortisation Rp135,726m = Rp1,710,733m (S5 p.128) leaves Rp30,361,232m of group cash operating cost; the other-activity cost of Rp668,374m is charged separately, leaving Rp29,692,858m of coal cash cost over 45.43 Mt (F1) = Rp653,597/t, which is the base from which other_cost_unit is struck. Realisation and royalty recompute exactly from F13/F11 (10.31%) and F13/F1 (0.5175); the remaining gap is the FY2026E fuel term in the cost split (C8), not a missing cost line.

flags.message: a.volume: bear -5 vs bull 0.5 is lopsided — mirror the shock or justify the asymmetry
flags.justification: The volume asymmetry is sourced in both directions: the bear cuts 5 Mt from the 9M shortfall (32.23 Mt, F36, S11) and the RKAB/DMO policy risk [S9, S10], while the bull adds only 0.5 Mt because the base already runs at the company's 49.5 Mt plan from FY2028E (F42, S11) and the add takes it to the 50 Mt RKAB-approved capacity exactly — a mirrored 1.05x bull would imply 52.5 Mt, above the 50 Mt RKAB-approved capacity (S3, S11), and is not sourced. The bull upside is carried on realised price, cost and payout instead.

flags.message: the price driver d.coal.newc must be shocked in both cases
flags.justification: d.coal.newc is not shocked directly because the engine's deck override flattens every later year onto the lt value (red-team challenge C1: an identity x1.0 reproduces a flat US$107.1 path to FY2095E instead of the deck's escalating path), so a benchmark shock would not sit on the base path. The price shock is carried on a.realisation, which multiplies the realised price against the same deck path in every year, including the lt-escalated years, so it is the path-consistent equivalent at the level the 9M print fixes (ASP +18% vs Newcastle +25%, F51, S11). The engine defect is escalated to the engine owner.

flags.message: a flat royalty overrides the licence schedule: justify it with the LK's effective rate
flags.justification: royalty_mode is flat at 10.31% because that is the rate the LK shows PTBA paying, not the top band of the schedule: royalties to government Rp4,322,659m on coal revenue Rp41,909,086m in FY2025A (F11/F13, S5 p.127-128) and Rp2,209,879m on Rp21,672,370m in H1-2026 (S6 Catatan 26/27a) = 10.20%. PTBA sells about half its volume domestically — 51.5% in 9M-2026 (F50, S11) and 54% in FY2025 (S7 p.65) — off a 2,800-6,100 GAR slate (F15), so its book mixes the low and mid tranches of the PP 19/2025 IUP schedule and the blended paid rate is the most-likely one. No scenario switches to the deck's banded royalty_iup_mid schedule: all three keep the flat effective rate, so the bull is not credited with the top band (which would tax its higher realised price more heavily). The 9M-2026 release reports cost of revenue up only 0.6% (F40, S11), consistent with a royalty charge that moves with realised prices, not with the top band. QC Q3 (round 1) is answered in report section 4 with the tail sensitivity: re-running the model on the deck's mid-band IUP schedule over the HBA reference, instead of the flat rate, lowers the life DCF by roughly a tenth. It is disclosed, not carried, because no observed year charges that band and the interim accounts show the same blended rate (S5, S6); the flat rate flatters the bull rather than the base.

flags.message: expected return +80%: name the two or three sourced drivers that produce it and what today's price implies (reverse DCF)
flags.justification: The expected return comes from three sourced drivers, none of them a stretched forecast. (i) The life-of-reserve DCF prices the 2,883 Mt reserve base (F5, S7 p.104) at the reviewed coal deck's mean-reverting Newcastle path through the 2026 measured realisation and the FY2025A calibration thereafter (S11/S5, F13/F1), so no spike ratio is carried into the long run; FY2026E volume is the 9M delivery (F36/S11) and the path returns to the company's 49.5 Mt plan from FY2027E (F42/S11), with the 50 Mt approved capacity reached only in the bull, so the near-term miss is not extrapolated and no above-capacity volume is assumed. (ii) The D&A restatement: the LK's real charge of Rp2,014,102m (F7, S5 p.159) instead of the data pack's Rp300,136m, on the LK operating profit Rp3,208,073m (F28, S5 p.17), rebuilds FY2025A EBITDA to Rp5,222bn, and the non-coal cost is charged once, not twice, lifting the recurring margin. (iii) The balance sheet the mining EV does not capture: net cash attributable to equity of about Rp3.0trn at 30 June 2026 after deducting the Rp1,304.8bn dividend payable (declared 11 June, paid 10 July 2026, F56/F57, S6 p.8 and Note 24), and the equity-accounted investments of Rp10,713.4bn at 30 Jun 2026 (S6 p.7); at 30 September, netting the DHE placements against the back-to-back loans leaves a similar figure (S11). The dividend payable is an explicit bridge deduction, so it is not counted as free cash. What today's price implies: the engine's reverse DCF is not used this round — its whole-path override flattens the deck's long-run escalation (red-team challenge C1, escalated to the engine owner), so a factor solved against that path is not on the base path. On the base path the price sits far below the DCF value of the reserve life; the two cross-check anchors (EV/EBITDA and dividend capacity) sit below the DCF because they capitalise near-term earnings and the payout, which is the honest caution carried in the bear case and the cross-check discussion. QC Q4 (round 1) asked for the price/NAV figure explicitly: section 4 now states that the price is about three-fifths of the life-of-reserve DCF, i.e. the market discounts well over a third of the base path before probability weighting (S0), and says the reverse DCF is restored when the engine path defect is fixed.
